title: Collective Responsibility and Individual Compensation
title_ja: 集団責任と個人への補償
abstract: This paper analyzes distributive justice in the presence of collective responsibility. We consider a society partitioned into groups, where three types of characteristics affect individual outcomes: circumstances for which neither individuals nor groups are responsible, collective responsible factors for which groups, but not individuals, bear responsibility, and personal responsible factors for which individuals are responsible. We propose two allocation rules: (i) group conditional equality and (ii) group egalitarian equivalence. Both solutions use a two-step procedure in which inter-group resource allocation is determined, and intra-group distribution second. This approach respects both individual agency within groups and collective responsibility across groups. We examine the basic properties of these allocation rules and offer axiomatic characterizations of them. For the characterizations, we extend the classical principles of natural reward and compensation developed by Marc Fleurbaey to the collective responsibility setting.
summary_ja: 個人や集団の責任外の環境、集団責任要因、個人責任要因の3特性が結果に影響する社会での分配的正義を分析する。
グループ間配分決定後にグループ内分配を行う、集団条件付平等と集団平等等価という2つの割当規則を提案する。
フルバエの自然な報酬と補償の原理を集団責任の設定へ拡張し、提案する割当規則の公理的特徴付けを与える。
reason_ja: 責任主義的正義論を集団責任へ拡張する公理的アプローチを学べるため。

title: Periodic Equity Prioritarianism
title_ja: 期間的公平優先主義
abstract: Abstract This paper engages with the question of how to understand prioritarianism when people are differently well off at different times. In this context, it introduces a new version of prioritarianism, periodic equity prioritarianism , which is inspired by how focusing on equally distributed equivalents can dissolve tensions in social evaluations that involve risk. The paper shows that periodic equity prioritarianism avoids both certain problems that timeslice prioritarianism faces and some problems that lifetime prioritarianism faces.
summary_ja: 個人が時期ごとに異なる厚生水準を持つ状況での優先主義（prioritarianism）の評価方法について考察する。
平等分配等価額（equally distributed equivalents）の概念に着想を得た「期間的公平優先主義」を導入する。
本手法がタイムスライス型や生涯型の優先主義が抱える評価上の問題を回避できることを示す。
reason_ja: 時点間の厚生評価に関する優先主義の新たな枠組みを把握できるため。

title: Bimodal spread majorization: bridging inequality, bipolarization, and polarization in income tax policy
title_ja: 双峰的拡大メジャライゼーション：所得税政策における不平等・二極化・極化の橋渡し
summary_ja: 【タイトルからの推測】メジャライゼーションの概念を双峰的拡大へと拡張する理論的分析と考えられる。
【タイトルからの推測】所得税政策における不平等、二極化、極化といった尺度間の関係を議論していると推測される。
【タイトルからの推測】税制設計を通じた所得分配評価手法の統一的な枠組みを提示していると思われる。
reason_ja: 所得税政策とメジャライゼーション理論の接点を学べる可能性があるため。

title: Poverty-reducing taxation with endogenous income
title_ja: 内生的所得を伴う貧困削減課税
summary_ja: 【タイトルからの推測】労働供給等の経済行動により所得が内生的に決まるモデルを扱っていると推測される。
【タイトルからの推測】内生的所得を考慮した上で貧困を削減するための最適な課税理論を分析していると見られる。
【タイトルからの推測】意思決定行動を踏まえた規範的課税政策の設計原理を論じていると考えられる。
reason_ja: 内生的所得形成のもとでの貧困削減と税制設計の理論を知るため。

title: Obvious Group Manipulations and Top Trading Cycles
title_ja: 明白な集団操作とTop Trading Cyclesメカニズム
abstract: We introduce a group version of non-obvious manipulability, which is stronger than the original definition by Troyan and Morrill (2020) and weaker than group strategy-proofness, and study its implications in Shapley-Scarf housing markets. We provide several characterizations of the Top Trading Cycles mechanism using the new condition.
summary_ja: 既存の非明白な操作可能性より強く集団戦略強靭性より弱い「明白な集団操作可能性」の集団版を導入する。
シャプレイ＝スカーフ住宅市場モデルを対象に、提案した新条件の影響を詳しく分析する。
新条件を用いることで、Top Trading Cycles（TTC）メカニズムの新たな公理的特徴付けを与える。
reason_ja: TTCメカニズムの耐戦略性と公理的特徴付けの最新進展を理解できるため。

title: On dynamic income taxation and absolute inequality
title_ja: 動的所得課税と絶対的不平等について
summary_ja: 本論文は動的所得課税と絶対的不平等（absolute inequality）の関係を分析した研究であると推測される。
動的な意思決定枠組みにおける最適課税モデルや不平等尺度の役割が議論されている可能性がある。
詳細な結果は要旨からは不明であるが、所得再分配に関する厚生理論的帰結を扱っていると思われる。
reason_ja: 動的所得再分配と絶対的不平等概念の関係に関心のある研究者に適しているため。

title: Motor precision shapes information seeking in perceptual decisions
title_ja: 運動精度が知覚的意思決定における情報探索行動を規定する
abstract: Adaptive behavior relies heavily on the confidence we have in our decisions. For instance, in the absence of explicit feedback, the confidence associated with a decision determines whether we seek additional evidence or are likely to change our mind. Recent studies suggest that confidence estimation also depends on motor processes involved in implementing perceptual decisions. However, whether motor-induced changes in confidence meaningfully affect behavior, such as by altering information-seeking, remains uncertain. The present study addresses this question. Participants performed a perceptual task requiring discrimination of the orientation of Gabor patches. The motor cost of the perceptual response was manipulated by varying the size of the response circles that participants had to reach to report their judgment. Consistent with previous findings showing that easier motor responses are associated with lower confidence ratings, we found that such responses were also linked to a greater tendency to seek additional evidence compared to more costly responses. Importantly, this increase in information-seeking behavior was not accompanied by any change in perceptual accuracy. These findings support the idea that the motor costs associated with perceptual decisions modulate confidence, and that such motor-induced changes in confidence play a functional role in guiding subsequent behavior.
summary_ja: 知覚的意思決定（perceptual decisions）における応答の運動コスト（motor costs）が確信度に与える影響を検証。
容易な運動応答は確信度（confidence）の低下を招き、正確さを損なわずに情報探索（information-seeking）を促進。
運動誘発的な確信度の変化が、その後の情報収集行動を調整する機能的役割を果たしていることを示した。
reason_ja: 意思決定における確信度形成と情報収集行動の運動メカニズムに関心がある研究者向け。

title: Economic burden of severe non-communicable diseases by level of care to inform priority-setting in Tanzania
title_ja: タンザニアでの優先順位設定に資する医療レベル別の重症非感染性疾患の経済的負担
abstract: Abstract Background Noncommunicable diseases (NCDs) account for nearly half of all deaths in Tanzania. To improve access to care for severe NCDs, Tanzania has introduced the PEN-Plus model at primary hospitals. However, evidence on the patient-level economic burden of severe NCD care across diseases and levels of care remains limited. This study estimated patient-level costs for rheumatic heart disease, sickle cell disease, type 1 diabetes mellitus, and type 2 diabetes mellitus and identified key drivers of cost variation. Methods A cross-sectional, prevalence-based cost-of-illness study was conducted among patients receiving outpatient care for type 1 diabetes, type 2 diabetes, rheumatic heart disease, and sickle cell disease at primary and tertiary hospitals in Tanzania. A bottom-up costing approach was used to estimate direct and indirect costs of outpatient care from the patients' perspective. Indirect costs were valued using the human capital approach. Socioeconomic inequality was assessed using concentration indices and generalised linear models with a log link; key drivers of cost variation were identified. Results We included 1,037 participants. The mean annual outpatient cost per patient was USD 255 (95% CI: 242–270). Direct non-medical and indirect costs accounted for most of the economic burden, with transport as the largest cost component (USD 87 per year). Costs varied by disease and level of care. Patients with sickle cell disease incurred the highest direct costs (USD 238 per year). For rheumatic heart disease, mean drug costs increased from USD 3 at primary hospitals to USD 65 per year at tertiary hospitals. Costs were lower at primary hospitals (CR 0.80; 95% CI: 0.72–0.90) and increased with distance travelled. Socioeconomic inequality was minimal at primary hospitals. In contrast, low-income groups had a statistically significantly higher share of patient costs among patients with type 2 diabetes and sickle cell disease attending tertiary hospitals. Conclusion The economic burden of severe NCD care in Tanzania is driven as much by access barriers as by medical costs. Expanding PEN-Plus, reducing transport-related costs, and aligning insurance benefits with long-term care needs could improve financial protection and equity.
summary_ja: タンザニアの医療機関で重症非感染性疾患患者の費用をボトムアップ法と人的資本法（human capital approach）で算出。
患者1人あたりの年間平均コストは255ドルで、交通費等の直接非医療費と間接費が負担の大部分を占めた。
低所得層の負担割合は三次病院で高く、優先順位設定（priority-setting）や医療の公平性向上への課題が示された。
reason_ja: 発展途上国における医療優先順位設定と経済的負担の公平性分析に関心がある研究者向け。

title: A Simple Proof of Koray's Theorem
title_ja: コレイの定理の簡潔な証明
abstract: In this note, I provide a direct and self-contained proof of Koray's (2000) theorem, by which a neutral and unanimous social choice function is universally self-selective if and only if it is dictatorial. Koray's (2000) original proof relies on results by Sen (1970) and Houthakker (1950) to construct a social welfare function for each alternative set. He then shows that these functions are Paretian and independent of irrelevant alternatives, allowing him to apply Arrow's (1950, 1951) impossibility theorem. Instead, I construct a cyclic preference profile and show that the voter who ranks the chosen alternative first is the dictator on every finite nonempty alternative set.
summary_ja: コレイ（Koray, 2000）の定理（中立・満場一致な社会選択関数の普遍的自己選択性と独裁性の同値性）の簡潔な証明を提示。
従来の証明はアローの不可能性定理（Arrow's impossibility theorem）等に依存していた。
本稿は巡回選好プロファイル（cyclic preference profile）を直接構築することで簡単な自己完結的証明を与えた。
reason_ja: 社会選択理論における自己選択性や不可能性定理の証明技法に関心を持つ研究者に最適。

title: Aggregating Rankings of Coalitions to Rank Individuals
title_ja: 個人の順位付けのための提携順位の集約
abstract: We develop an ordinal framework for aggregating a profile of rankings of coalitional performances to determine the ranking of individuals. From university ratings to the assessment of team-sports players, we often evaluate individuals based on their coalitional performances. Although such evaluation has been addressed by cooperative game theory, it is only recently that its ordinal counterpart, social ranking theory (Moretti, 2015), has emerged. As most of the literature considers a single coalitional ranking (which corresponds to a real-valued characteristic function), we extend the model to allow a profile of coalitional rankings (which corresponds to a multidimensional characteristic function). We tackle the aggregation problem by introducing three families of inter-profile axioms, each representing how the rankings should interact or contribute to the output. After revealing fundamental impossibilities concerning the reconciliation of different families, we characterize a new solution, Pareto-extension Lex-cel (PEL), via some weaker versions of the inter-profile axioms. PEL extends Lex-cel, which is a central solution in social ranking theory, by analogy with Sen's Pareto extension rule. Our results develop the connection between classical Arrovian aggregation, cooperative game theory, and social ranking theory.
summary_ja: 提携パフォーマンスの順位プロファイルを集約して個人の順位を決定する順序的枠組みを提案。
提携順位の拡張に伴うプロファイル間公理を導入し、公理間の矛盾を示す不可能性定理（impossibility theorem）を導出。
センのパレート拡張ルールに依拠し、社会順位理論（social ranking theory）の新規解PELを公理化した。
reason_ja: 協力ゲーム理論とアロー型集約理論を融合した社会順位理論の拡張に関心がある研究者向け。

title: Safe manipulation of tops-only voting rules
title_ja: Tops-only投票ルールにおける安全な操作可能性
abstract: We study tops-only voting rules on the domain of all preferences with a unique top, focusing on manipulation by risk-avoiding voters. Following Hartman et al.(2025), we measure resistance to manipulation by the RAT-degree: the minimum number of other voters' reports that a voter needs to observe for a ``safe'' manipulation to become possible. Given the observed reports, such a manipulation weakly improves on truthful reporting under every completion of the unobserved reports and strictly improves on it under at least one completion. For any finite set of at least three alternatives, we show that anonymity, unanimity, and winner monotonicity imply an upper bound of $\lceil n/2\rceil$ on the RAT-degree, where $n$ is the number of voters. We provide exact characterizations of the RAT-degree for anonymous generalized median voter schemes and voting by quotas, without imposing single-peakedness or separability on preferences. For odd $n$, the median voter rule and objectwise majority rule uniquely maximize the RAT-degree within their respective classes and attain the general upper bound.
summary_ja: リスク回避的投票者による「安全な操作」に対するTops-only投票ルールの耐性を評価した論文。
操作に必要な他者の投票観察数の最小値（RAT度）を定義し、一般的な上限がceil(n/2)であることを証明。
一般化メディアンルール等のRAT度を特定し、奇数人ではメディアンルールが上限を達成することを示した。
reason_ja: リスク回避的な戦略操作への耐性を測る度合いや境界条件に関心がある研究者におすすめ。

title: Veto Proportionality in Multiwinner Voting with Ranked Preferences
title_ja: 順位付き選好を持つ多勝者投票における拒否の比例性
abstract: Proportional representation in committee voting with ranked preferences requires voter groups to influence the selected committee in proportion to their size. Existing axioms, such as proportionality for solid coalitions (PSC), demand that like-minded groups of voters are entitled to elect a fair number of candidates to the committee. However, in applications where voters are collectively affected by the entire committee, it may be equally important that no group is confronted with a disproportionate number of candidates that it regards as undesirable. Motivated by this, we initiate the study of veto proportionality in committee elections with ranked preferences. Our central notion, the proportional multiwinner veto core (PMVC), generalizes Moulin's proportional singlewinner veto core to multiwinner elections by allowing groups of voters to partially veto sets of candidates. We analyze how the PMVC relates to existing fairness notions and design rules that are guaranteed to select committees from the PMVC. Specifically, we first introduce a duality framework that connects inclusion- and exclusion-based fairness notions and show, e.g., that the dual axiom of the PMVC strengthens PSC. We further show that STV satisfies the dual axiom of the PMVC, which also implies the existence of committees in the PMVC. Subject to a strengthening of committee monotonicity, we characterize the rules that always return committees in the PMVC as sequential adaptations of singlewinner voting rules that always select from the proportional singlewinner veto core. By our duality framework, this also gives rise to a new class of rules that satisfy PSC. We further prove that the dual axiom of the PMVC and RankPJR+ are jointly satisfiable, thereby pushing the frontier of fairness guarantees that can always be attained. Finally, we show that deciding whether a given committee belongs to the PMVC is coNP-complete.
summary_ja: 多勝者投票において望ましくない候補の排除に着目し「拒否の比例性（PMVC）」を提案した論文。
包含的・排除的公平性を結ぶ双対性枠組みを構築し、STVがPMVCの双対公理を満たすこと等を示した。
PMVCを満たすルールの順次構造による特徴付けや、委員会がPMVCに属するかの判定のcoNP完全性を証明。
reason_ja: 多勝者投票における比例的公平性の新公理や拒否コアに関心のある研究者におすすめ。

title: An axiomatic foundation for optimized certainty equivalents
title_ja: 最適化確実性等価の公理的基礎
abstract: Optimized Certainty Equivalents (OCEs) are an important class of risk measures for optimization and risk management that includes the Mean--Variance criterion, Expected Shortfall, the Entropic Risk Measure, and expectation. Despite their importance, economic axioms have not characterized OCEs. We propose a new axiom called Fair-Coin Compensation, which characterizes OCEs together with Strong Risk Aversion and Normalization. We interpret Fair-Coin Compensation through the fair assignment of two losses by a coin toss: transfers between two participants can remove the additional risk created by the random assignment. Adding further axioms yields sharper characterizations. Monotonicity yields standard OCEs; Positive Homogeneity, together with Prudence, yields Expected Shortfall; and Fair-Coin Independence yields the Entropic Risk Measure. We also axiomatize the Mean--Variance criterion using our novel axiom of Equal-Mean Randomization, which states that random assignment of two losses with the same expected value does not produce a risk measure above the average of their risk measures.
summary_ja: リスク管理で重要な最適化確実性等価（OCE）の経済的公理化を初めて達成した論文。
新公理「公平なコイン補償」等を提案し、OCEやExpected Shortfall等の特徴付けを与えた。
さらに新公理「等平均ランダム化」を導入することで、平均・分散基準の公理的導出にも成功した。
reason_ja: リスク尺度や意思決定理論における確実性等価の公理的導出に関心がある研究者におすすめ。

title: Biseparable representations of the Certainty Equivalents
title_ja: 確実性等価の双分離型表現
summary_ja: （推測）要旨未記載のためタイトルからの推測だが、確実性等価の双分離型表現を分析した論文と思われる。
（推測）意思決定理論におけるリスク下の選好や評価尺度の数学的構造を扱っていると推測される。
（推測）確実性等価表現の公理的・関数的性質の解明を目指していると考えられる。
reason_ja: 確実性等価の関数表現や意思決定理論における選好表現に関心のある研究者におすすめ。

title: Obvious group manipulations in voting
title_ja: 投票における明白な集団操作
abstract: We study obvious group manipulation in voting and characterize it as manipulation identifiable from a coalition's option sets alone. Our analysis focuses on two overlapping classes: tops-only rules and rules satisfying the majority criterion, including all Condorcet-consistent rules. On the universal domain with at least three alternatives, a tops-only rule is not obviously manipulable by groups (NOMG) if and only if it is dictatorial. For rules satisfying the majority criterion, NOMG is impossible when $n,m\geq3$, except with four voters and three alternatives. We quantify the coalition sizes behind these restrictions, obtaining sharp bounds for efficient tops-only rules and an exact threshold for majority-criterion rules with odd electorates. In the exceptional configuration, we characterize an interval of NOMG scoring rules containing Borda, which is also Condorcet consistent there. We further characterize NOMG with two alternatives and apply our tops-only characterization to generalized median voter schemes and voting by committees.
summary_ja: 集団の選択肢集合のみから識別可能な「明白な集団操作」の理論的分析を行った論文。
Tops-onlyルールでは明白な集団操作不能（NOMG）を満たすのは独裁的ルールのみと証明。
多数決基準を満たすルールにおけるNOMGの不可能性や、例外的な設定でのボルダ実行可能性等を解明。
reason_ja: 明白な戦略操作可能性の集団拡張や各種投票ルールの理論的限界に関心のある研究者におすすめ。

title: Proportional Representation for Almost-Solid Coalitions and the Proportional Veto Core for Rankings
abstract: A proportional ranking should give groups of voters representation commensurate with their size at every prefix. Proportionality for solid coalitions (PSC) provides this guarantee to groups whose members rank the same set of candidates above all others. How much representation should a group receive when a few outside candidates disrupt that agreement? We extend the proportional veto core to rankings through candidatewise and setwise guarantees. We show that setwise veto protection is equivalent to robust Rank-PSC under reversal of both the voters' preferences and the collective ranking. Robust Rank-PSC extends representation guarantees to almost-solid coalitions at every prefix. Each distinct outside candidate that disrupts a coalition's agreement reduces its guaranteed representation by at most one, and this bound is tight. Using reverse-sequential variants of Ordered Phragmén and STV, we construct rankings satisfying robust Rank-PSC$+$ in polynomial time. This stronger axiom preserves the guarantee after deleting any suffix of the collective ranking and restricting voters' preferences to the remaining candidates. Verifying robust Rank-PSC is coNP-complete, whereas verifying robust Rank-PSC$+$ takes polynomial time. We also introduce Rank-Aligned PJR$+$, which requires the first $r$ candidates of the collective ranking to satisfy PJR$+$ when each voter approves their top $r$ candidates. We give a polynomial-time algorithm that meets this requirement simultaneously for every $r$. For fixed-size committees, the Expanding Approvals Rule guarantees Rank-PJR$+$ but can violate robust PSC regardless of how ties are broken or payments are assigned. We give a modification that satisfies both guarantees for any prescribed committee size.

title: Truthful compromise and insurance on a sphere
abstract: Can public choice without transfers insure conflicting interests when action intensity is fixed? We require truthful reporting for every increasing-concave evaluation of alignment with private ideals. On a sphere, efficiency at profiles with at most three ideal directions forces fixed-weight random dictatorship; weaker tests suffice in two and three dimensions. From four dimensions, binary efficiency permits committees to insure members by placing outcome risk orthogonally to their reports. We identify restrictions shared by all mechanisms with these incentives and binary efficiency: binary winning probabilities determine mean outcomes at every profile and individual alignment distributions at planar three-camp profiles. When these probabilities depend only on camp size, complete insurance at balanced equilateral disagreement requires dimension proportional to population. In contrast, committees reduce each participant's welfare loss relative to certain zero alignment to any prescribed positive fraction of the equal-weight random-dictatorship loss in a population-independent dimension.

title: Knowing Less After a Diagnostic Test: Dilation in Clinical Decision-Making
abstract: Dilation (Seidenfeld and Wasserman 1993) occurs when conditioning on new information \textit{only} increases uncertainty regardless of what the information reveals. Often viewed as an undesirable feature of models of ambiguity, dilation has sparked sustained debate about belief updating. This paper shows that following established clinical guidance can induce dilation, even for diagnostic tests that meet conventional performance benchmarks. We characterize when a test is dilation-inducing and show that a ubiquitous feature of performance studies -- evaluating tests against an imperfect reference -- creates scope for dilation. To facilitate detection before clinical use and inform regulatory standards, we develop a finite-sample valid hypothesis test of the null that a diagnostic test is dilation-inducing in this context. Applying the method to an influential study that preceded and contributed to the clinical adoption of chest CT screening for COVID-19, we find that the data are consistent with dilation.

title: Nash implementation of dynamic matching rules
Shill-proof rules in object allocation problems with money
abstract: We consider the object allocation problem with money. The seller owns multiple units of an object and is solely interested in her revenue from an allocation. Each buyer can receive at most one unit of the object and has preferences over pairs consisting of consumption of the object and payments, which are not necessarily quasi-linear. We study the seller's incentives to increase her revenue by introducing false-name buyers, a practice commonly referred to as shill bidding. An (allocation) rule is shill-proof if the seller cannot increase the revenue by introducing false-name buyers. A rule is a price-based weak priority rule if there is a profile of prices such that buyers who are willing to receive the object at their own prices do so in descending order of price. We establish that a rule is revenue undominated among the class of rules satisfying shill-proofness, strategy-proofness, and non-imposition if and only if it is a price-based weak priority rule. Our result provides justification for the use of posted-price rules—widely adopted by online marketplaces, and internet auctions as ``buy-it-now'' auctions—over auction-type rules in terms of shill-proofness.

title: An Enforcement Foundation for Constrained Equal Awards
abstract: Standard claims problems take claims as given. We ask how rule selection changes when a certified claim can be augmented by a privately known component that is costly to verify. In a binary environment, equal treatment of equals, claim boundedness, and efficiency impose a sharp lower bound on the gain from exaggeration and hence on the expected auditing needed for truthful reporting to be weakly dominant. The constrained equal awards (CEA) rule attains this bound at every report profile through a correlated audit policy. Conversely, every profilewise audit-minimal rule is CEA. The pointwise result also makes CEA the unique admissible rule that minimizes expected verification cost under every prior over true claims.

title: Cognitive Constraints and Misspecification Concern
abstract: We study repeated decision problems in which an agent has cognitive constraints and is concerned that her models might be misspecified. She first uses data to weight candidate models, subject to a cognitive-capacity constraint on the complexity she can process, and then she evaluates choices according to how well they perform under those models. More data need not overcome limited capacity: a statistically inferior but simpler model can remain relevant in the long run. When the constraint binds, evidence that favors models in proportion to their complexity can leave current behavior unchanged while still affecting later responses to data. This constraint eliminates cycles between risky and safe actions when simple models favor safety, and relaxing it can make risky play more attractive initially yet less frequent in the long run. It can also sustain misspecified model classes by suppressing choices that would reveal their errors.

title: Distortion in Online Voting
abstract: We initiate the study of distortion in online voting, a framework that bridges computational social choice and online algorithms. In contrast to the classical offline setting, where the full election instance is known in advance, we consider a dynamic environment where a fixed set of voters is present from the beginning, but alternatives arrive sequentially over time. Upon each arrival, a mechanism must immediately and irrevocably decide whether to retain the currently selected candidate or switch to the newly arriving one, operating solely on the partial ordinal rankings induced by the underlying cardinal preferences. We provide upper and lower bounds for deterministic and randomized mechanisms under two standard cardinal preference frameworks. Utilitarian framework: For deterministic mechanisms under adversarial arrival order, we establish an $Ω(mn)$ lower bound and give an matching online algorithm with distortion at most $\frac{2}{3}m(n+\frac{1}{4})$. For randomized rules, we introduce regularity, which allows any regular, order-independent offline randomized rule to be converted into an online rule with the same expected distortion. The Harmonic voting rule satisfies this property, yielding online distortion $O(\sqrt{m\log m})$. Metric framework: For deterministic mechanisms, maintaining an alternative within a $\varphi$-weighted uncovered set guarantees distortion $2+\sqrt{5}$. We show that matching-based offline rules achieving distortion $3$ cannot be directly implemented online. We establish a lower bound of $\sqrt{13}$, even with three alternatives, and a matching upper bound for three alternatives and any number of voters. For randomized mechanisms, regularity gives an online distortion of $3-\frac{2}{n}$ via Random Dictatorship.

title: Orchestrating the Distributive Process: Baron and Ferejohn Meet Tullock
Multidimensional mechanism design and robust revenue maximization in multi-object auctions
Strong Nash equilibria of core-selecting double auctions
abstract: We study core-selecting auctions for double auctions that incorporate package bidding. Unlike in one-sided core-selecting auctions, the core may be empty in more general double auction settings, and truncation strategies need not be amongst a bidder’s best responses. Nevertheless, we establish the existence of a core-selecting auction in which every imputation in the core with respect to true preferences corresponds to a strong Nash equilibrium. Specifically, for any core imputation, there exists a profile of truncation strategies that constitutes a strong Nash equilibrium and induces precisely that imputation.

title: Disenfranchisement in Spatial Voting Games
abstract: The questions of voting rights, group membership, and the boundaries of acceptable discourse all involve a recursive, self-stability issue, wherein the voters, group members, and acceptable commentators are often the ultimate arbiters of their own rules for inclusion and exclusion. In order to understand how ideological or issue diversity may impact the stability of such inclusion and exclusion, we introduce franchise elections, where voting members of a group vote to change the electorate. In particular, when agents are positioned inside an ideological or issue space, a social choice function that aggregates agent viewpoints induces a preference for agents over group composition, where agents prefer groups that improve the social choice function outcome for them. We demonstrate that when ideological space is two-dimensional, these franchise elections can generate complex behavior and that this complexity exists for any social choice function. Using the Yolk social choice function from voting theory, we illustrate that franchise elections can predict that agents attempting to introduce a new ideological axis perpendicular to an existing left-right spectrum risk disenfranchisement unless they ally with either side of the spectrum, and that franchise elections can cycle with any period.

title: Are Revealed Preferences All You Need for AI Alignment?
abstract: AI agents learn what principals want from what principals choose. We offer a criterion for when a principal's decisions, at every belief an AI might hold, are all the AI needs. For acting, they are. Cautious actions, such as deferring to a person, typically divide the principal's actions into blocks, and for choosing costless evidence, decisions are enough exactly when the same evidence is best in every block. Otherwise, the AI acts as its principal would yet can gather the wrong evidence, and greater capability can turn that error into incorrect actions. Choices between two mistakes reveal what decisions miss.

title: Nearly Settling the Complexity of Connected $\varepsilon$-Envy-Free Cake Cutting
abstract: Envy-free cake cutting has been one of the central problems in fair division. In cake cutting, agents' preferences over the cake are accessed through Robertson--Webb (RW) queries. For three or more agents, no algorithm that makes finitely many RW queries can always find a contiguous, exactly envy-free allocation. For contiguous $\varepsilon$-envy-free allocations, however, Hollender and Rubinstein~(JACM, 2025) showed that $\poly(\log(1/\varepsilon))$ RW queries suffice for four agents, leaving open whether such a bound is possible for five or more agents. In this paper, we establish a striking change in query complexity: $\poly(\log(1/\varepsilon))$ RW queries suffice for up to five agents, whereas $(1/\varepsilon)^{Ω(1)}$ queries are necessary for seven or more agents, even when valuations are additive. Thus, we resolve the five-agent case and, more broadly, determine whether polylogarithmic query complexity is possible for every number of agents except six. We also explore the computational complexity of finding contiguous $\varepsilon$-envy-free allocations. When monotone Lipschitz valuations are given by polynomial-time evaluation procedures (e.g., arithmetic circuits and efficiently computable Turing machines), we show that an $\varepsilon$-envy-free division can be computed in polynomial time for five agents. In contrast, even for additive valuations, finding an $\varepsilon$-envy-free division is UEOPL-hard for every fixed number of agents $n\ge7$ and PPAD-complete for every fixed $n\ge13$.

title: Weighted Proportional Toll Sharing on General Highway Networks
abstract: We extend the Segments Equal Sharing (SES) method of \citet{wu2024} from line highways to general highway networks, including networks with cycles. The input is an exogenously specified profile of route flows. We introduce the Weighted Proportional Sharing (WPS) method, which distributes each route's mileage revenue in proportion to weighted segment lengths and its fixed-surcharge revenue in proportion to positive segment surcharges. Route SES is recovered under homogeneous weights within each revenue component. We show that WPS is the sum of two weighted Shapley allocations and that the underlying route games extend the dividend and Shapley representation of linear SES. Two axiomatic characterizations identify WPS. The first uses additivity and proportional treatment of segments used on every positive-revenue route. The second combines sub-highway efficiency and weighted average balanced contributions under a route cancellation rule. We also extend Segments Proportional Sharing to general networks, identify it with the $τ$ value of the corresponding route game, and characterize it axiomatically. For Segments Compensated Sharing we characterize a weighted average tree allocation by consistency across rooted branch settlements and averaging under a specified root lottery. A cyclic example shows that different route splits can change the allocation even when origin--destination volumes and aggregate toll revenue are held fixed.

title: Reserve Systems in Dynamic Settings: Account Design and Inherited Rights
abstract: Research on reserve systems mainly considers static settings, formulating and studying choice rules for a given allocation problem. Dynamic settings are different in that the problem is not given. Over time, more positions become available, and each time the institution must build the current problem from its past. We distinguish the ledger, which stores information about earlier allocations, the account, which transforms these data into the current problem, and the choice rule, which selects an outcome for that problem. The same choice rule can implement very different policies under different accounts. If each new batch is assigned while holding earlier recipients and their categories fixed, then as batches shrink, over-and-above, the most generous reserve policy we study, can select nearly the same recipients as minimum guarantee, the most conservative one. Cumulative implementation uses a different account, which reconsiders the categories of earlier recipients, and prevents this compression. We characterize it by resource-release invariance. With arrivals or changes in priorities, the ordinary choice rule might reject an earlier recipient whose appointment has to be honored. We introduce and characterize retain, reassign, and boost (RRB) choice rules, under which every incumbent retains her appointment and can have her category changed. Combining RRB with individual-proposing deferred acceptance gives a strategy-proof mechanism under which each incumbent keeps her appointment or receives one she prefers. Applications include waiting lists in school and university admissions, public recruitment, and court-ordered corrections.

title: Temporal Fair Division: Simultaneous Guarantees for Goods and Chores
abstract: We study temporal fair division of indivisible items in both the goods and chores settings, with $n \ge 2$ agents and nonnegative additive values or costs. Items arrive one at a time and must be assigned immediately and irrevocably. The arrival order and all agents' values or costs are known in advance, and the cumulative allocation must satisfy the fairness requirements after each arrival. For goods, we give a polynomial-time algorithm that simultaneously achieves exact temporal proportionality up to one item (TPROP1), a $1/n$ approximation to temporal maximin share (TMMS), and a $1/(n-1)$ approximation to temporal envy-freeness up to one item (TEF1). The TMMS factor is optimal. For chores, we give a polynomial-time algorithm that simultaneously achieves exact TPROP1 and a $2-1/n$ approximation to TMMS. Classical scheduling lower bounds based on fixed sequences carry over to chores TMMS, establishing the optimality of this factor for $n=2,3$. For every $n \ge 2$, we further show that $2-1/n$ is the optimal TMMS factor subject to exact TPROP1. For every fixed $n \ge 3$ and every finite $β\ge 1$, we construct an instance of chores admitting no $β$-TEF1 allocation.

title: Closing Gaps in Temporal Fair Division for Chores
abstract: We study the fair division of indivisible chores that must be assigned in a prescribed order. The complete instance is known in advance, but assignments cannot be changed. Temporal envy-freeness up to one chore (TEF1) requires envy-freeness up to one chore after every arrival. For goods, TEF1 allocations need not exist, and deciding whether one exists is NP-hard. For chores, Elkind et al. (AAMAS 2025) showed that TEF1 allocations exist for two agents, but left open whether they always exist, conjecturing that they do not, and whether deciding their existence is hard. We resolve both questions, confirming the conjecture in a strong form: for every $n\ge3$ and every finite factor, some $n$-agent instance admits no allocation satisfying TEF1 even up to that factor. This holds even when all agents have the same multiset of individual chore costs, with nine chores sufficing for three agents. Deciding TEF1 existence is NP-complete for every fixed $n\ge3$, even when all costs lie within a factor $1+2^{-m}$ of one another, where $m$ is the number of chores. Instances without TEF1 allocations exist arbitrarily close to the uniform cost matrix with $O(n\log n)$ chores, and just nineteen for three agents. We then relate fairness to social cost. Even when a TEF1 allocation is supplied, minimizing social cost subject to TEF1 admits no polynomial-time approximation within any factor polynomial in the number of chores unless P$=$NP, already for three agents with strictly positive normalized costs. In contrast, for every fixed number of agents, we give an FPTAS for the optimal temporal EF1 factor, the smallest factor up to which TEF1 can be satisfied, whose output has social cost no larger than that of the cheapest allocation attaining this factor. Thus a slight relaxation of fairness permits a social-cost guarantee that, unless P$=$NP, no polynomial-time algorithm can provide under exact TEF1.

title: Signaling in repeated delegation
Random Utility Models in the Consumption-Budget Setting: Vertex and Network-Flow Characterizations
abstract: This note supplements our paper \textit{Alternative Computational Formulations for Testing Discrete-Choice Random Utility Models: Half-Space and Network-Flow Formulations} and serves two purposes: 1. We clarify the conceptual distinctions between two classes of random utility models (RUM): those in the consumption-budget setting \citep{kitamura2019nonparametric} (hereafter KS) and those in the finite-alternative setting (e.g., Chapter~7 of \cite{chambers2016revealed}). In particular, we show (Theorem 1) that each rational type, as defined in KS, can be obtained as a coordinate projection of the deterministic choice vector induced by a strict preference ranking that satisfies what we call a patch-monotonicity condition. 2. We generalize the network-flow characterization for finite-alternative RUM in \cite{fiorini2004short} to the consumption-budget setting (Theorem 2). Specifically, we show that a vector of choice probabilities in the consumption-budget setting is rationalizable in the KS sense if and only if it is the image of a unit flow on a multi-arc powerset digraph under a fixed linear map. The key distinction is that our digraph allows multiple arcs between the same pair of nodes, whereas the digraph in Fiorini has at most one arc between any pair of nodes.

title: Intransigence or compromise: concatenated opinion dynamics with voting feedback
abstract: In this paper, we study opinion evolution in a sequence of Friedkin-Johnsen (FJ) models, concatenated so that the final opinions of each model serve as the initial opinions of the next. Each FJ model is followed by a vote, and each agent becomes partially or fully stubborn in the next model, depending on how close its opinion is to the voting result. With the state-dependent switching of stubbornness, the dynamics are not guaranteed to be contractive. We show that, over any fixed strongly connected network, the opinions always converge. A sufficient condition on the initial opinions is proposed, under which consensus is reached exponentially fast. For the complete graph, we further show that, if the agents' stubbornness levels do not differ too much, an agent that is partially stubborn in one FJ model can never become fully stubborn in a subsequent one: once it has started compromising, it keeps doing so.

title: Mechanism Design and Active Systems Theory: 60 Years of Parallel Development
abstract: The survey compares two research traditions within the mathematical theory of designing the rules of interaction (mechanisms) for purposeful participants: mechanism design, together with contract theory and implementation theory, and the theory of active systems created by V.N. Burkov and developed into the theory of control in organizations (TCO) by D.A. Novikov's school; the main results of Yu.B. Germeier's school and of the domestic schools adjacent to active systems theory (AST) are covered as well. The problem statements and principal results of 2006-2026 are presented: for mechanism design (MD) - robust and dynamic mechanism design, multidimensional screening, information design, simplicity of mechanisms and credibility of the designer, market design, algorithmic and learning-based design, mechanisms for AI agents, and robust, relational, dynamic and algorithmic contracts; for AST and TCO - a general typology of control, strategy-proof and incentive-compatible planning mechanisms, decomposition of the agents' game, systems with distributed control and coalitional interaction, reflexive games and informational control, control of staff and structure, dynamic active systems, and project management. A correspondence between the classical results is established (the fair play principle and the revelation principle, the serial resource allocation mechanism and the uniform rule, active expertise mechanisms and generalized median schemes, quasi-compensatory incentive schemes and contracts under observable actions), and priorities are delineated by uniform rules; the areas where the two traditions diverge are identified, as are the dimensions of the problem (staff, structure, institutions, awareness, agents' beliefs) covered only by TCO.

title: A Polynomial-Time Algorithm for Constant-Factor EFX Allocations of Chores
abstract: We study the fair division of indivisible chores among agents with additive disutilities, focusing on the central fairness notion of envy-freeness up to any chore (EFX), and its multiplicative approximations. Although the existence of constant-factor approximations to EFX are known, computing such an allocation in polynomial time remained open. We resolve this question by giving an algorithm that, for every $\varepsilon\in(0,1)$, computes a $(3+\varepsilon)$-EFX allocation in time polynomial in the input length and $1/\varepsilon$. Our result relies on two algorithmic contributions. First, we give a fully polynomial-time approximation scheme (FPTAS) for earning-restricted (ER) equilibria with equal earning requirements and arbitrary feasible chore earning limits. We develop a new nonconvex program with chore payouts and money-flow variables, and prove that every local maximum yields an exact ER equilibrium. We then give a mirror-ascent algorithm for this program and prove that it converges to an approximate ER equilibrium in polynomial time. Second, we give a new procedure that converts the approximate equilibrium into a $(3+\varepsilon)$-EFX-friendly allocation, a suitable starting point for the chore-swap framework of Garg and Murhekar (2026). The procedure uses a flexible price threshold to choose swap chores and their recipients together, overcoming a factor-four bottleneck in the earlier approaches while accommodating approximate earnings. We expect these ideas to be useful more broadly in fair division, including for goods and other fairness notions.

title: Expanding and Evaluating the Applicability of Safe Pareto Improvements
abstract: Even when players can make credible joint commitments in games, disagreement about the game's default outcome (e.g., about equilibrium selection) can prevent them from agreeing on any particular payoff profile. We study safe Pareto improvements (SPIs): commitments that sidestep this obstacle by inducing a new game that is isomorphic to the original (after iteratively removing strictly dominated actions) but entrywise Pareto better. We do so by constructing token games: cheap-talk games rendered meaningful by commitments to take payoff-relevant actions (in prior work, strategies in the original game) as a function of the token outcome. Since these token games preserve the original game's strategic structure, players should expect them to be played isomorphically and hence agree that they Pareto improve on the original. In this work, we study token game SPIs under three additional commitment abilities: (1) burning utility, (2) transferring utility between players, and (3) transferring utility with an outside party conditional on the token outcome (e.g., via insurance-like contracts). We characterize when SPIs exist in each case and give efficient algorithms for optimizing over them. Finally, we propose evaluating SPI frameworks by how often they enable SPIs in randomly generated games. In such experiments, our methods substantially outperform prior work.

title: Computing EF1 Allocations with Few Value Queries
abstract: We give a deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that allocates $m$ indivisible goods among $n$ agents with nonnegative additive valuations using $O(n^5\log^2 m)$ value queries and guarantees envy-freeness up to one good (EF1). Concurrent work of Lin, Liu, Tao, and Zhou achieves $O(n^8\log m)$ comparison queries, attaining the optimal $O(\log m)$ dependence on $m$ for fixed $n$. Each comparison query can be simulated using two value queries, so their bound also holds for value queries. Our contributions are a much simpler algorithm and proofs, and polynomial-time computation.

title: Reasoning about risk and the Sure-thing Postulate
title_ja: リスクに関する推論と確実性原則（Sure-thing Postulate）
abstract: Savage’s normative model of rational decision-making is deficient because the Sure-thing Postulate systematically ignores important information contained in lotteries. Useful statistical facts about lotteries, such as their modes and medians, are available as defeasible reasons for reasoned choices between lotteries. Because such summary statistics are holistic properties of lotteries, we can find cases where appealing to facts about modes and medians as normative reasons for choosing between lotteries conflicts with Savage’s Sure-thing Postulate. Such cases show the Sure-thing Postulate to be implausible and undermine both Savage’s argument for subjective expected utility theory and his argument for Bayesian subjective probabilism.
summary_ja: サヴェッジの意思決定モデルにおける確実性原則が、宝くじの統計的性質を無視している点を批判的に検討した。
最頻値や中央値といった宝くじの全体的な統計情報は、合理的な選択の根拠となり得ることを示した。
これらの統計情報への訴求が確実性原則と矛盾する場合があることを示し、主観的期待効用理論の妥当性に疑問を投げかけた。
reason_ja: 意思決定理論の基礎となる公理の妥当性を再考する議論を提供しているため。

title: On the Complexity of Envy Cycle Elimination
abstract: The envy cycle elimination (ECE) algorithm is a fundamental algorithm for the fair allocation of indivisible goods, guaranteeing an allocation that is envy-free up to one good under arbitrary monotone utilities. We show that the ECE algorithm can be implemented in $O(nm)$ time for $n$ agents and $m$ goods, and establish the tightness of this bound.

title: Folk Theorems for Social Learning
abstract: We study repeated games with purely informational externalities. Each player observes a single conditionally independent signal and then repeatedly takes publicly observed actions to maximize their expected discounted payoff, which depends only on the state and their own action. We show that, when there are sufficiently many players and they are sufficiently patient, there exist equilibria where information is aggregated: the players' payoffs approximate the full-information payoff. This holds even if actions are uninformative under myopic play. Conversely, even if myopic play reveals the state, there also exist equilibria where information is not aggregated: payoffs approximate those under autarky. Our results speak to the range of possible outcomes of social learning games with forward-looking agents.

title: Ordinal Hegselmann-Krause Systems
abstract: We study opinion formation in the popular Hegselmann-Krause model when agents replace the traditional averaging update by a median update or more general ordinal aggregation methods. We analyze the convergence properties of synchronous and asynchronous dynamics. For asynchronous dynamics, we show that every HKS with a $1$-Lipschitz ordinal aggregation function converges in worst-case time $\mathcal{O}(n^4)$. For the special case of median aggregation and for the family of $k\textsf{-large}$ aggregation functions, in which agents select the $k$-th largest opinion in their neighborhood, we obtain sharper bounds of $\mathcal{O}(n^3)$. For general ordinal aggregation, some sequence of $\mathcal{O}(n^2)$ updates reaches an equilibrium from every initial state. Nevertheless, other update sequences may cycle, and uniform random activation can require exponentially many updates with overwhelming probability. For synchronous dynamics, we obtain a tight characterization. Ordinal aggregation functions satisfying the $1$-Lipschitz condition are shown to guarantee convergence in linear time. This result applies to many natural examples such as minimum, maximum, median, and $k\textsf{-large}$ functions. When the Lipschitz condition is violated, there exist instances in which synchronous dynamics do not converge at all.

title: Entry Deterrence with Public Signals: Revisiting the Chain-Store Paradox
abstract: We revisit the classic chain-store paradox by introducing exogenous public signals about the incumbent's private type that arrive each period over a finite horizon. We fully characterize perfect Bayesian equilibria in terms of sequences of reputation cutoffs that increase over time: entrants enter below their cutoff, while the normal incumbent mixes below its cutoff and fights above it. The equilibrium outcome is generically unique. Information arrival dampens the incentive to build a reputation, so full deterrence need not emerge as the horizon grows arbitrarily long, even when the incumbent is very patient. We characterize exactly when there is full deterrence in the limit, along with the limiting equilibrium when there is not.

title: Path-Independent Deleveraging Rules
abstract: We characterise path-independent auto-deleveraging (ADL) rules as an extended log-exponential family. Immunity to account splitting, merging and reopening further restrict the class. Homogeneity (essentially) restricts the class to a one-parameter family ordered by both fairness and platform risk. Its split-proof members continuously interpolate between proportional division and water-filling. Among these rules, decreasing the parameter reduces risk at the cost of increasing inequality in how accounts are treated. This suggests selecting the parameter through an ex-ante calibration to a risk bound on historical data to choose a maximally fair rule subject to that bound. A counterfactual replay of Hyperliquid's ADL episode on 10 October 2025 finds that a range of intermediate parameters significantly improves on the observed allocation in both burden dispersion and subsequent risk statistics.

title: Moral Inversion: Expressive Payoffs and the Reliability of Consensus
abstract: Moral inversion is a public consensus on an account that falsely reverses responsibility for a harm. We study how expressive payoffs affect its emergence in a sequential social-learning model. A larger payoff makes an account more attractive to endorse, but also makes each endorsement of that account weaker evidence in its favor. We show that under a single-peakedness condition on private beliefs a larger payoff both increases the probability of an incorrect consensus on the favored account and reduces its reliability. Without this condition, both comparisons can reverse, and the informativeness of the public record can strictly improve in the Blackwell order. Finally, we show that a sufficiently large increase in the expressive payoff nevertheless restores the benchmark comparative statics.

title: Moral AI and the Erosion of Its Own Demand
abstract: We study the evolution of human preference frequencies and AI adoption when individuals can choose between a moral AI that rules out defection and an unconstrained AI that preserves discretion. By allowing users to commit to cooperation, moral AI can sustain cooperation even when cooperative preferences are too scarce to do so on their own. But this success has a cost. By turning otherwise dormant cooperative preferences into committed behavior, moral AI exposes its users to exploitation by selfish individuals, causing the population share of conditional cooperators to decline under evolutionary selection. As conditional cooperators become less prevalent, equilibrium adoption eventually converges to zero. Moral AI can therefore be self-liquidating. For initial shares between the moral-AI adoption cutoff and the threshold for cooperation without AI, moral AI generates cooperation while lowering the limiting share of conditional cooperators. Adoption ultimately vanishes, leaving a lower share of the preference type that initially sustained demand for commitment.

title: Pareto-Optimal and Strategyproof Data-Sharing Between Competitors
abstract: We study data-sharing among firms competing in the same market through the quality of their predictive models. We model firms' profit through two main components, precision and market share, where the former depends on the firm's own number of datapoints and the latter depends on the endowments of all firms. We characterize Pareto-optimal contracts as those in which at least one firm receives all of the other firms' datapoints. We then propose a parametric family of data-sharing contracts and show that, under any of them, the relative market shares of all firms remain constant, eliminating the negative effect of sharing data with competitors and equalizing all firms' gains relative to the no-sharing scenario. We further show that one contract within this family satisfies both Pareto-optimality and strategyproofness against firms attempting to under-declare the size of their initial endowment. Finally, using a real-world dataset, we empirically test the gain in profit for all firms under the contract described above, and show that data-sharing is particularly beneficial when the machine learning task is harder or when firms' initial endowments are closer to homogeneous.

title: Two is better than one: optimizing binary rating scales for online platforms
abstract: Online platforms often struggle with inflated, uninformative user ratings. This issue can be mitigated by better design of the data collection mechanism, for example through changing the phrasing of user questions. Previous work optimizes a single rating scale to best distinguish the inherent qualities of items under binary feedback. In this paper, we demonstrate the power of utilizing different rating scales for different users. First, we show that a designer can always split a single rating scale into two to improve item rankings. Next, we formally characterize the optimal design of multiple scales as a series of 0-1 step functions whose threshold values are evenly spaced. Finally, we consider an adaptive model where subsequent rating scales can depend on the responses from previous users and items are ranked by their full sequence of responses, and show that adaptivity leads to exponentially greater distinguishing power. All in all, our theoretical results show that using multiple rating scales significantly improves item rankings on platforms.

title: The Optimal Competitive Ratio for Subadditive Online Combinatorial Auctions is Less Than 1/2
abstract: We construct a four-buyer online combinatorial auction with independent subadditive valuations and a fixed, known arrival order in which every online rule earns strictly less than $1/2$ of the expected offline optimum. A common partition, revealed at the third arrival, gives the first three buyers one unit of welfare per item. If the rule uses three distinct partitions, either an item allocated early contributes zero or the fourth buyer's expected value for the remaining bundle is one less than its size. We compute the optimal online and offline welfare exactly and show that a $1/2$ guarantee always holds with at most three buyers.

title: Sequential Contract Design for Budgeted Crowdsourcing
abstract: A principal wishes to crowdsource a collection of tasks under a fixed compensation budget. The quality of a task's outcome is stochastic and depends on the worker's effort level. Since this effort is unobservable, the principal offers contracts to workers specifying their compensation for each possible outcome. The principal offers these contracts sequentially, using previously observed outcomes and payments to decide whom to approach next and what contract to offer. The objective is to maximize the expected value of the work produced while ensuring that total payments never exceed the budget, regardless of the realized outcomes. Contract design must therefore account both for a worker's incentives and for the budget available to incentivize others. For valuations that are additive across tasks, we characterize how the approximability of the optimal adaptive policy depends on the numbers of workers, effort levels, and outcomes. Polynomial-time constant-factor approximation is possible whenever the number of workers, effort levels per worker, or outcomes per task is constant, but impossible in general when all three are unrestricted, unless $P=NP$. We obtain tight guarantees for every fixed number of workers, establish computational hardness even in restricted settings, and obtain exact algorithms and approximation schemes in more structured settings. We also investigate simple contract structures, demonstrating both the benefits of adapting contracts to previous outcomes and the limitations of local contract rules, while identifying conditions under which a local policy achieves a constant-factor guarantee. Finally, we extend our analysis beyond additive valuations, obtaining constant-factor approximations for monotone submodular valuations with binary outcomes, including guarantees against a stronger full-knowledge benchmark under additional assumptions.

title: Measuring ambiguity attitudes without incentives: evidence from an introspection-based method
title_ja: インセンティブなしでの曖昧さ態度の測定：内省に基づく方法からの証拠
summary_ja: 本研究はタイトルから、金銭的報酬なしで曖昧さ態度（ambiguity attitude）を測定する手法を検討していると推測される。
内省（introspection）に基づく評価方法を用いて、個人の選好測定における実行可能性や妥当性を分析していると思われる。
実験経済学や意思決定論におけるインセンティブの必要性に関する議論に寄与していると考えられる。
reason_ja: 曖昧さ態度や意思決定の測定手法に関心を持つ研究者に適している。

title: Priority-swapping-proof allocation
title_ja: 優先順位の交換に対して頑健な配分
summary_ja: 本研究はタイトルから、優先順位の交換（priority swapping）に対する耐性を持つ配分ルールを分析していると推測される。
メカニズム設計において、個人の優先順位の操作や入れ替えを防ぐための論理的条件を検討していると思われる。
公平性や効率性を満たしつつ頑健性を備えた配分メカニズムの理論的性質を明示していると考えられる。
reason_ja: 配分問題やメカニズム設計における耐戦略性を追究する研究者に適する。

title: Cursed Equilibria and Knightian Uncertainty in a Trading Game
title_ja: 取引ゲームにおける呪われた平衡とナイツ的不確実性
summary_ja: 本研究はタイトルから、取引ゲームにおける呪われた平衡（cursed equilibrium）とナイツ的不確実性の影響を推測する。
情報非対称性下でのプレイヤーの認知バイアスと曖昧さ（Knightian uncertainty）の相互作用を解析していると思われる。
限定合理的な意思決定と曖昧さが市場取引の均衡に及ぼす影響を理論的に解明していると考えられる。
reason_ja: 曖昧さ下の意思決定や限定合理性ゲーム理論を研究する層におすすめ。

title: Aggregation in networks
title_ja: ネットワークにおける集約
summary_ja: 本研究はタイトルから、ネットワーク構造上における選好や情報の集約（aggregation）について分析していると推測される。
構造的相互作用を持つエージェント間での集約ルールや意思決定の理論的性質を検討していると思われる。
社会選択理論における集約問題をネットワーク理論の視点から拡張していると考えられる。
reason_ja: ネットワーク上の社会的選択や情報集約理論を専門とする研究者に適する。

title: Efficiency with Political Power Dynamics and Costly Policy Change
title_ja: 政治的力学の動態とコストを伴う政策変更下での効率性
summary_ja: 本研究はタイトルから、政治的権力の動態とコストを伴う政策変更の下での効率性（efficiency）を考察していると推測される。
権力の移動や政策転換の摩擦が社会的な資源配分や動学的決定に及ぼす影響を検討していると思われる。
制度設計や政治的選好集約における動学的効率性の成立条件を分析していると考えられる。
reason_ja: 政治的選択や動学的メカニズム設計を研究する意思決定理論家に適する。

title: Empowering Women, Empowering Energy: The Role of Intra-household Bargaining Power in Alleviating Multidimensional Energy Poverty in Rural China
title_ja: 女性のエンパワーメントとエネルギー：中国農村部における多次元エネルギー貧困緩和に対する世帯内交渉力の役割
abstract: Improving women’s intra-household bargaining power (IHBP) and reducing energy poverty in rural areas contribute to achieving the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals, such as achieving gender equality, empowering all women and girls (Goal 5), and ensuring access to affordable, reliable, sustainable, and modern energy for all (Goal 7). This study explores the impact of rural women’s IHBP on multidimensional energy poverty (MEP), using data from the 2014-2020 China Family Panel Studies and a conditional mixed-process model. We construct a composite index to measure rural women’s IHBP, accounting for dimensions of asset ownership, labor allocation/labor market participation, household financial management, household expenditure allocation, and household decision-making power. Our results suggest that women’s IHBP is negatively and significantly associated with household MEP. A one-unit increase in rural women’s IHBP is associated with an 8.0-percentage-point reduction in the probability of household MEP. The negative association between women’s IHBP and MEP remains stable across male- and female-headed households, although the estimates for the two subgroups do not differ significantly. Meanwhile, all variables used to construct women’s IHBP are negatively and significantly associated with MEP. The mediation analysis suggests that women’s IHBP is associated with lower MEP incidence through increased household income and reduced use of non-clean energy. Our findings remind policymakers that they should pay more attention to empowering rural women in their efforts to reduce energy poverty.
summary_ja: 2014-2020年の中国家庭パネル調査データを用い、農村女性の世帯内交渉力が多次元エネルギー貧困に与える影響を分析した。
世帯内交渉力の尺度が1単位上昇すると、多次元エネルギー貧困（MEP）の発生可能性が8.0%ポイント減少することが判明した。
媒介分析により、世帯所得の向上や非クリーンエネルギー利用の減少を経由してエネルギー貧困が緩和されることが示された。
reason_ja: 多次元貧困測定や世帯内不平等の実証に関心を持つ研究者に直接役立つため。

title: Equal opportunities in school choice settings
title_ja: 学校選択制度における機会均等
abstract: We introduce a novel notion of fairness, inspired by the equality of opportunity literature, into the school choice setting, endowed with a measure of the match qualities between students and schools. In this framework, fairness considerations are made by a social evaluator based on the match quality distribution. We impose the standard notion of stability as a minimal desideratum and study matchings that satisfy our notion of fairness and an efficiency requirement based on aggregate match quality. To overcome some of the identified incompatibilities, we relax the fairness and efficiency definitions, and embed them in a family of linear social welfare functions. We then propose an algorithm that maximize social welfare over the set of stable matchings. Finally, we illustrate our approach with an application to the allocation of Italian high school students in the 2021/2022 academic year. JEL: C78, D63
summary_ja: 機会均等の概念を学校選択に導入し、生徒と学校のマッチングの質（マッチクオリティ）の分布に基づく新たな公平性を定義した。
安定性を前提条件とし、公平性と総マッチング品質による効率性を両立させる配分を考察し、概念間の不整合性を整理した。
定義を緩和した線形社会福祉関数を設定し、安定マッチング集合上で社会福祉を最大化するアルゴリズムを提案・適用した。
reason_ja: 機会均等の理論を実際の制度設計や政策の最適化へ応用する研究であるため。

title: No NEET to Worry? Parental Background and Italian Graduates’ Transition to Employment
title_ja: ニートの心配は無用か？親の背景とイタリアの大学卒業生の就業への移行
summary_ja: 【タイトルからの推測】親の背景がイタリアの大学卒業生における就職・就労への移行に与える影響を分析した論文と推測される。
【タイトルからの推測】卒業生のニート（NEET）化リスクと親の社会経済的背景との関連性を検証していると考えられる。
【タイトルからの推測】高等教育修了後の労働市場移行における親の階層による格差や機会不平等を考察していると思われる。
reason_ja: 【推測】家庭背景による機会の不平等や労働市場移行の実証に関わるため。

title: Fair division with binary valuations: Characterizations
title_ja: 2値評価における公平分配の特徴づけ
abstract: We consider the fair allocation of indivisible goods with binary valuations. In this setting, the maximum Nash welfare rule, the leximin rule, and all additive welfarist rules with a strictly concave function coincide. We show that for any number of agents, this rule is the only rule that satisfies envy-freeness up to one good, strategyproofness, neutrality, minimal completeness, and invariance under disapproving unassigned goods (IDU). Moreover, we present an alternative characterization for two agents, where we replace IDU with non-redundancy and resource-monotonicity. In both characterizations, all axioms are necessary.
summary_ja: 2値評価の不可分財分配では最大ナッシュ福祉、レキシミン、厳密凹関数型福祉の各規則が一致する。
本研究は同規則がEF1、戦略頑健性、中立性、最小完全性、IDUを満たす唯一のルールであると証明した。
2代理人ケースでは非冗長性と資源単調性を用いた別の特徴づけを与え、全公理の必要性を示した。
reason_ja: 2値評価分配問題における代表的ルールの公理的特徴づけを学べるため。

title: Strategy-proofness, Pareto efficiency, and sign proportionality in budget aggregation with strictly convex norm-induced preferences: An impossibility result
title_ja: 厳密に凸なノルム誘導選好を持つ予算集約における戦略強靭性、パレート効率性、符号比例性：不可能定理
summary_ja: （タイトルからの推測）厳密に凸なノルム誘導選好を持つ代理人の予算集約問題を扱っていると推測される。
戦略強靭性とパレート効率性、符号比例性という望ましい属性の同時充足可能性を検討しているとみられる。
これらの公理を同時に満たす集約規則が存在しないことを示す不可能定理を提示していると推測される。
reason_ja: 予算集約における主要公理の同時充足不可能性（不可能定理）を把握できるため。
